definitions.gloss: before one knows, unnoticed, without realizing
definitions.explanation: Describes something that happens gradually or subtly without the speaker noticing when or how it occurred.

examples.japanese: いつのまにか{雨|あめ}が{止|や}んでいた。
examples.english: Before I knew it, the rain had stopped.

examples.japanese: いつのまにか{子供|こども}たちは{大人|おとな}になった。
examples.english: Before we knew it, the children had grown up.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はいつのまにか{部屋|へや}からいなくなっていた。
examples.english: She had left the room without anyone noticing.

notes:
USAGE: いつのまにか emphasizes that the speaker did not notice the process or moment of change. Often used with past tense and ていた form.

POSITION: Usually appears at the beginning of a sentence or before the verb phrase.

COMPONENTS:
・いつ (when) + の (possessive) + {間|ま} (interval) + に (at) + か (question/uncertainty)
・Literally: 'at what point in time (unknown)'

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{知|し}らないうちに - without knowing
・{気|き}がつかないうちに - without noticing
・いつしか - before one knows (more literary)
